{}.semantics: The enclosed value is interpreted as a reference to a document or data source defined in the Input_Data section. The value may be a simple identifier or a qualified reference.

[].semantics: Identifies a dataset, variable, or dataset-qualified variable referenced by the specification. Interpret the enclosed value according to the first matching pattern.

patterns.semantics: References the specified variable without explicitly identifying its dataset. The dataset MUST be resolved from the current execution context.
References the specified dataset as a complete data object.
References the specified variable within the explicitly identified dataset.

@.name: Data Reference
@.meaning: References a named document, data source, or a specific member of that source defined in the Input_Data section.

resolution.source: The identifier immediately following @ MUST resolve to an entry defined in Input_Data.
resolution.member: When a member identifier follows the source, separated by a period, it MUST resolve within the referenced source.
resolution.whole_source: When no member is specified, the reference resolves to the complete source.

semantics.scope: References are resolved against Input_Data for the current specification.

evaluation.timing: The reference is resolved when the containing instruction is evaluated.
evaluation.substitution: The resolved value is supplied to the instruction in place of the reference.
evaluation.mutation: Resolving a reference does not modify the referenced source.

constraints: The source identifier MUST exist in Input_Data.
A member identifier MAY only be used when the referenced source exposes that member.
Source and member identifiers are case-sensitive.
A reference MUST NOT contain whitespace.
A reference MUST contain no more than one member separator.

errors.undefined_source: Raised when the source identifier is not defined in Input_Data.
errors.undefined_member: Raised when the requested member does not exist within the resolved source.
errors.invalid_reference: Raised when the reference does not conform to the defined pattern.
errors.unavailable_source: Raised when the source is defined but cannot be accessed.

examples.resolves_to: The member VAR within the Input_Data source named Library.
The complete Input_Data source named Library.
The complete Input_Data source named Var.
The complete Input_Data source named Document.

/xx/.meaning: Short codes for instructions - used to identify specific actions or parameters within the specification.

D:.meaning: Can only be present in the Input_Data section. It is used to define a Document that can be referenced in the specification.
semantics: The value following D: identifies a document available to the specification.
Documents may contain metadata, derivation standards, controlled terminology, or implementation guidance.
If a referenced document contains metadata definitions, those definitions become available for validation.
Variables referenced in Logic, Validation, Output, or FINAL instructions must exist in at least one applicable metadata source when such metadata is supplied.
A variable reference that cannot be resolved against supplied metadata must raise a validation error.

:.meaning: Indicates the end of an instruction

phrases.semantics: Marks the beginning of a named specification block. The supplied identifier is the unique name for the block.
Marks the end of a specification block. More than one block may be defined in a single file.

semantics: Contains execution actions to be performed after all specification blocks have completed.
Execution actions are processed sequentially in the order specified.
If an action is not defined in final_actions, execution must stop with an error.
Actions may consume outputs generated by preceding blocks.
The result of each action becomes available to subsequent actions.
Only one FINAL instruction may exist in a specification.

phrases.semantics: Defines the intended objective of the specification.

Defines the language in which the executable output must be generated. There can be only one LANGUAGE_TARGET instruction in a single specification block. LANGEUAGE_TARGET is not optional. If not specified, the default target language is SAS additionally the target language must be the same for all blocks in a single specification file.
Identifies data used as input to the specification. The data may be referenced by name or by a data object reference.
Defines logic that must be implemented in the generated output.

phrases.meaning: Variable or output to be produced by the block
phrases.semantics: Identifies the variable or output to be produced or modified by the specification.
Defines rules to validate the variables that are used in the logic.

phrases.meaning: General instructions or notes for the block
semantics: Instructions of what to do in case of ambiguous, unclear or incomplete requirements or when data needs to be queried to data management.
When Notes contains instructions to generate ADRG text, the ADRG output must describe only the implemented derivation logic.
Validation checks, execution errors, specification issues, warnings, assumptions, and implementation diagnostics must not be included in ADRG text unless explicitly requested.
ADRG text must be generated independently of validation reporting.

rules: Every OPEN must have a matching CLOSE.
OPEN and CLOSE block names must match.
Block names must be unique within a file.
Only one FINAL instruction may exist.
FINAL must appear after all blocks have been closed.
At least one FINAL instruction must be present.
If no FINAL instruction is present, the specification is invalid.
No instructions may appear after FINAL.
